subject.title: [BUG] OpenAI Codex errors leak into user chat

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this as a parser/sanitizer bug only, or also silently suppress unconfigured Codex/provider failures at the provider/routing boundary?
rationale: The `detail` parser gap is a bounded bug, but silent discard changes observable failed-turn behavior and diagnostics across provider routing, subagents, and channel delivery.

options.title: Parser plus explicit routing policy
options.body: Add `detail` parser coverage and define when unconfigured-provider failures become no-reply versus safe generic user-facing copy, with tests for both assistant-error and sanitizer delivery paths.

options.title: Parser-only repair
options.body: Treat this issue as a raw-JSON formatting bug now and track silent unconfigured-provider suppression separately after maintainers choose the policy.

options.title: Require live trigger proof first
options.body: Keep the current generic assistant-error mitigation and wait for a fresh Telegram/live reproduction before changing parser or routing behavior.

recommendation.title: Parser plus explicit routing policy
recommendation.body: Add `detail` parser coverage and define when unconfigured-provider failures become no-reply versus safe generic user-facing copy, with tests for both assistant-error and sanitizer delivery paths.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete merged and refined the current raw-provider-error suppression policy and is the strongest history-backed owner for the remaining user-visible failure semantics decision.
